dimension: D09-testing — Missing/weak testing strategy; designs not demonstrably testable

findings.finding: No mockable-vs-real-agent boundary is defined for the harness adapters, so the contract-test suite (§14) cannot actually run in CI. Both Claude Code AND Codex are MVP-blocking (ADR-006), and both require authenticated, paid, non-deterministic, network-bound CLIs that churn fast (TR-02/TR-03). The draft says 'a shared HarnessAdapter conformance suite run against both Claude and Codex ... pin agent CLI versions and re-run on bump' but never specifies what the suite runs against: live agents, recorded fixtures, or a fake transport. Without a defined seam (e.g. a recorded-transcript / recorded-JSON-RPC replay layer between the adapter and the real CLI), the conformance suite is either flaky+costly (real agents) or nonexistent. This is the single biggest testability hole because the two adapters are the most fragile, most-churning, MVP-blocking surface in the system.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 'Adapter contract tests' bullet; ADR-006 (both harnesses MVP-blocking, status from SDK stream / app-server push); RISKS TR-02 (Codex app-server 'partly experimental', schema churn), TR-03 (Claude SDK/statusLine/JSONL churn, total_input_tokens semantics changed at v2.1.132). No doc states which adapter tests are mock-driven vs require a real Claude/Codex install + account.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Testing Strategy: add a 'Test seam & mockability' subsection that locks a recorded-interaction boundary per adapter — (a) Claude: golden SDK-message-stream + statusLine-JSON + transcript-JSONL fixtures per pinned CLI version, fed through the adapter's stream-status/telemetry/read-transcript contract with the real CLI mocked out; (b) Codex: a recorded app-server JSON-RPC session (request/response/notification log) replayed over a fake stdio TokioChildProcess. Declare conformance tests run in CI against fixtures (deterministic, no account); a separate, manually-triggered 'live-agent smoke' tier runs against real pinned CLIs and is NOT a merge gate. State the CI schema-regen job (OQ-HARN-SPIKE-4) diffs the pinned schema and fails red on drift.

findings.finding: The highest-rated risk in the whole plan — detached-daemon restart + session resume/survival (TR-01, critical/high) — has no deterministic test design. §14 reduces it to one line ('the hardest, needs real-session QA'), effectively punting the #1 risk to manual testing. There is no fault-injection seam to kill the daemon mid-operation, no injectable clock to make lease expiry / heartbeat-staleness deterministic, no fake PTY to assert orphan/zombie reaping (TR-07), and no harness to assert 'resume restores the session vs replay+relaunch fallback' without spawning real agents. As specified these become exactly the flaky integration tests the dimension warns against.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 'Terminal tests' and 'Lease/concurrency tests' bullets; RISKS TR-01 test signal ('Kill the daemon mid-/tdd run ... assert resume restores, scrollback-replay is readable, no orphaned PTY children'), TR-06 ('two owners contend ... across a simulated daemon restart'), TR-07 ('Crash-kill the daemon (SIGKILL) mid-session; assert no orphaned agent CLI/sidecar/PTY survives'), TR-13 (single-instance / stale-socket / version-skew test signals). None of these are reflected as a testable harness design in §14; ADR-008 makes lease expiry time-based ('probabilistic') with no injectable-clock requirement for tests.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Testing Strategy + §Session Lifecycle & Survival: mandate three architectural seams FOR TESTABILITY and bind them as invariants: (1) an injectable Clock/time source so lease TTL, heartbeat staleness, and 'stale' status transitions are driven by a fake clock (no sleeps) — makes TR-01/TR-06/heartbeat-poller tests deterministic; (2) a fault-injection hook on the daemon supervisor that can SIGKILL/abort the write-actor and PTY manager at named checkpoints (mid-apply, post-event-pre-projection, mid-execute) so crash-recovery and resume-or-replay are unit/integration-testable; (3) a FakePty / FakeHarness implementing the HarnessAdapter contract so survival, orphan-reaping, and resume-vs-replay logic are tested without real agents. Define daemon-restart tests as recovery-of-state assertions over the event store, not process-resurrection assertions.

findings.finding: Alt-screen / raw-mode TUI reattach fidelity — explicitly called 'the hardest correctness problem' and 'lossy' — has no defined verification corpus or pass/fail criterion. §14 says 'scrollback serialize/replay fidelity for alt-screen/raw-mode TUIs ... needs real-session QA', and TR-01 mentions 'snapshot-diff serialized VT state against ground truth', but there is no golden-VT-snapshot fixture set, no definition of what 'readable (not garbled)' means as an assertion, and no statement of which fidelity guarantee MVP actually commits to (OQ-PLAT-6 is still an open spike). A correctness property described only as 'QA against real Claude/Codex' is untestable in CI and unfalsifiable as written.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 'Terminal tests'; ADR-009 (headless VT state model, backpressure mandatory); ADR-010 ('accurate alt-screen/raw-mode TUI re-attach is lossy'); RISKS TR-01 ('snapshot-diff serialized VT state against ground truth', test tagged [research required]); OPEN_QUESTIONS OQ-PLAT-6 (terminal-state-recovery still a pre-build SPIKE, status SPIKE).
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Terminal Subsystem + §Testing Strategy: require a recorded-PTY-byte-stream corpus (captured raw output of real Claude/Codex alt-screen runs, committed as test fixtures) replayed through the headless VT — the test asserts the serialized VT snapshot byte-for-byte (or cell-grid) matches a committed golden, removing the live agent from the loop. State the exact MVP fidelity guarantee per harness (resolve OQ-PLAT-6: live-reconnect-while-daemon-alive = lossless scrollback; daemon-restart = labeled 'restored view, process relaunched') so the UI never over-promises, and so 'pass' is a concrete, asserted snapshot rather than human eyeballing.

findings.finding: §14 lists fail-closed-on-audit-write and fencing-token rejection but does not specify how to make them DETERMINISTIC. Fail-closed requires injecting an audit/event-write failure mid-transaction (the executor must abort the mutation if the audit row can't commit); fencing-token rejection requires forcing a stale-token holder to attempt a mutation after lease expiry. Neither is testable without (a) a fault-injection point on the event-store write and (b) the injectable clock from the survival finding. The behaviors are named as goals but the mechanism that makes them assertable is missing.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 'Gateway tests' ('stale-precondition re-check, fencing-token rejection of stale holders, fail-closed-on-audit-write'); ACTION_GATEWAY §4.1 'no invisible mutation' / §16.4 stale preconditions / §17 audit; RISKS TR-06 (executor rejects stale fencing token); ADR-003 (event + outbox + projection in one txn — the txn boundary is exactly where fail-closed must be tested).
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Event Store & Concurrency Model + §Action Gateway Executors + §Testing Strategy: state that the single-writer write path exposes a test-only fault injector (fail the events/outbox/projection txn at a chosen phase) so a fail-closed test asserts the mutation did NOT apply when the audit write fails (atomicity). Require every executor to take the fencing token as an explicit parameter and reject lower-than-current tokens, with a property test on monotonicity and a stale-token-rejection unit test driven by the fake clock + reclaim-bumped token. Add a 'preview == applied mutation' equivalence test for git executors (PR-03 test signal) — preview-then-apply diff must equal the actual mutation.

findings.finding: Determinism prerequisites for the event-sourced core are unstated. ULIDs (22 shared IDs), timestamps, monotonic fencing tokens, and idempotency-key derivation (action type + canonical resource ref + payload hash) all embed nondeterministic/clock-dependent inputs. The golden-event-log projection tests (§14) and idempotency-dedup tests can only be stable if these sources are injectable. The draft never requires injectable ID/clock/hash sources, so the very first test category ('golden event logs -> rebuild projections -> assert read models') is at risk of nondeterminism.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 'Event-store/projection tests' + 'Gateway tests' (idempotency dedup); §5 (22 shared IDs = prefixed ULIDs); OQ-GW-8 (idempotency key = action type + canonical resource ref + payload hash); ADR-008 (monotonic fencing token); EVENT_MODEL (append-only seq-ordered events).
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Domain Model / §Testing Strategy: add a 'Determinism for testability' invariant — all ID minting, time, and randomness flow through injectable providers (IdGen, Clock), seedable in tests so event logs and projections are reproducible. Specify the canonicalization rule for idempotency-key payload hashing (stable field ordering, normalized whitespace) and add a test that two semantically-identical requests produce the same key (dedup) while a changed param does not.

findings.finding: No frontend / UI / Tauri-IPC testing strategy exists at all. §14 is entirely daemon-side. The MVP ships 20 screens, a projection-driven reattaching client, xterm.js over a Tauri Channel, attention-first ordering, structured approval cards outside terminal text, and graph-with-list-fallback (§11, UX §8/§9). None of this has a test plan: no component tests, no projection-rendering tests, no reattach-after-UI-restart test, no terminal backpressure/flow-control UX test, no demo-path e2e harness for the WebView. The 'Demo integration test' bullet asserts the PRD §25 path end-to-end but gives zero mechanism for driving the Tauri UI.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 (all bullets daemon-internal; only 'Demo integration test: the PRD §25 path end-to-end' touches UI, with no method); §11 (20 screens, xterm.js WebGL, Tauri Channel, backpressure); RISKS PR-02 test signal references status fixtures but not UI; OQ-UX-7 (xterm.js flow-control UX: 30fps batch, XON/XOFF, 50MB cap, 'output throttled' indicator) has no test.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Frontend Architecture + §Testing Strategy: add a frontend test tier — (1) pure projection-view component tests over fixture projections (attention-ordering, degraded states, approval-card rendering, graph list-fallback) with the UDS client mocked; (2) a UI-restart reattach test that points the WebView at a mock GatewayPort and asserts the client re-renders live state without writing the DB; (3) a backpressure UX test driving a high-rate byte stream into the terminal channel and asserting the throttle indicator + bounded buffer. State how the PRD §25 demo e2e is driven (e.g. WebDriver/Tauri driver against a daemon seeded with FakeHarness) so the demo integration test is mechanizable, not aspirational.

findings.finding: The build-gating load test (OQ-DATA-SPIKE-3 / TR-05, SQLite single-writer contention) has no pass/fail threshold, so it is untestable as written. The risk register asks to 'measure write-queue depth, p95 intent-commit latency, and reader latency ... assert reads stay sub-100ms while writes queue' and 'quantify the ceiling', but no UX latency budget or concurrent-agent target (N) is committed in the architecture. A load test with no acceptance number cannot pass or fail; it just produces a graph. OPEN_QUESTIONS explicitly says ARCHITECTURE.md must state the number before freezing single-writer.
findings.evidence: RISKS TR-05 test signal ('start at N=20 ... quantify the ceiling and document it; assert reads stay sub-100ms'); OPEN_QUESTIONS OQ-DATA-4 / §13 step 1 ('What is the documented concurrent-agent write-throughput ceiling, and at what N does intent-commit p95 exceed the UX budget? Needs the load test before ARCHITECTURE.md states a number'); ADR-003 'What Would Change This' (contention making single-writer a bottleneck — must quantify). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 has NO load-test bullet at all despite this being a build-gating spike.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Event Store & Concurrency Model + §Testing Strategy: add a load-test entry with committed thresholds — target N concurrent mutating agents (e.g. N=20 MVP), p95 intent-commit-latency budget (state the number), and reader-latency SLO (sub-100ms) as the assertion. Make the load test a defined gate (run before single-writer freeze; document the measured ceiling in the doc). Without a number the spike cannot be closed.

findings.finding: §14 has no structure: no test pyramid / tier definition, no statement of what is a merge-blocking CI gate vs nightly vs manual, no coverage or 'no task without a test scenario' rule, and no mapping from the 13 TR-* / 10 PR-* 'Test / validation signal' entries (the project's richest test material) into the testing section. The result is that the most valuable test specs live in RISKS.md and are not load-bearing in the architecture. tasks-gen is instructed to attach happy/edge/error/integration scenarios per task, but the architecture gives it no test taxonomy to bind to.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 is a flat 8-bullet list tagged [PROPOSED] with no tiers/gates/coverage; RISKS.md every TR-01..13 and PR-01..10 row carries a concrete 'Test / validation signal' column none of which §14 references; PR-01 mitigation ('no task without a spec anchor') has no test-coverage analog; CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF lists 'missing tests' as a gap-audit dimension.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Testing Strategy: restructure into explicit tiers (unit / contract-with-fixtures / daemon-integration-with-fakes / live-agent-smoke / demo-e2e / security / load), mark which tier is a merge-blocking CI gate, and add a traceability table mapping each TR-*/PR-* test signal to a tier + owning module. Add the rule 'every architecture invariant has at least one falsifiable test' (e.g. TR-10's 'Brain seam has no import/handle path to the SQLite writer or executors' as a static/architecture invariant test).

findings.finding: Security/redaction tests are listed but several MVP-blocking security invariants are undertested or untestable as stated. 'Redaction-before-persist' and 'secrets never in events' need a property/fuzz test (token-shaped strings injected into every event-emitting path must never appear unredacted in the store), but §14 only asserts the happy case. The Brain over-reach invariant (TR-10: 'no code path lets a Brain tool write SQLite or call an executor directly') is an architecture/static-analysis test, not a runtime one, and §14 does not call it out. Command-injection (TR-09: stdin not argv, 10MB cap) has fixtures in RISKS but no §14 entry tying them to the adapter boundary.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 'Security tests' (redaction-before-persist; secrets never in events; injection via stdin not argv; Codex rollout 0600); RISKS TR-09 (injection fixtures, 10MB cap), TR-10 ('architecture invariant test' — no Brain path to writer/executors), TR-08 (assert stat 0600 on rollout JSONL); OQ-SEC-2/5 (redaction + sensitivity tiers MVP-blocking).
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Testing Strategy + §Trust Boundary: specify (1) a redaction property test that fuzzes secret-shaped inputs through every event/preview/audit path and asserts zero unredacted leaks; (2) a static/architecture invariant test (compile-time module boundary or dependency-graph assertion) proving the Brain seam crate cannot reach the eventstore-writer or executor crates; (3) the TR-08 post-session stat==0600 assertion and TR-09 injection-fixture + 10MB-cap rejection test bound to the adapter input path. These convert security goals into falsifiable checks.

findings.finding: Migration and projection-rebuild testing is mentioned ('migration round-trips', 'crash-recovery interrupt mid-apply -> replay -> consistent') but the event-schema-versioning story it depends on is still OPEN (OQ-DATA-9), so the test cannot be fully specified. There is also no forward/back-compat test for tolerant event readers, and no test that a projection rebuilt from scratch equals an incrementally-folded projection (the core event-sourcing safety property).
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 'Event-store/projection tests' (golden logs, crash-recovery, migration round-trips); OQ-DATA-9 (event schema versioning still OPEN, MVP-blocking); ADR-003 ('corrupt projection -> drop & replay'); EVENT_MODEL §13 projection rebuild.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Event Store + §Testing Strategy: add a 'rebuild equivalence' invariant test (full replay projection == incremental projection for the same event log) and a tolerant-reader test (older + newer schema-versioned events both fold correctly) once OQ-DATA-9's envelope-versioning is locked. Make schema-version round-trip part of the migration test set.
